reason: A: the 'CLINICALLY TESTED' eyebrow has fallen below the CTA and floats alone. The headline breaks into a 5-line stack with 'days' orphaned on the last line. The jar and logo are shrunk to tiny side-by-side thumbnails, so the product and brand are almost lost. The legal copy is a long, cramped column. Still, it reads headline → body → CTA in the right order. B: the legal paragraph sits at the very top, above the headline, which badly breaks the reading order. The eyebrow comes after the body copy, and the tiny logo sits between the copy and the leaf image. The CTA is cut off from its copy by the leaf block, and the jar is dropped to the bottom edge like an afterthought. B's order is more jumbled, so A is less bad.

A keeps the original three-column structure intact with clean hierarchy and a well-placed CTA. Its flaws are minor: the slightly taller canvas leaves loose vertical padding, and the headphone headband now crowds the ear cups. B is broken: the oversized headline fights the date card for attention, and the body copy is squeezed into a gap between the card and the headphones. The ear cups spill outside their circle, the RSVP button collides with the circle's edge, and the reading order is jumbled (headline → date → copy → CTA scattered across the canvas).

A breaks the composition: the can is pulled off the yellow circle and jammed into the top edge, 'Grab a Can' has lost its button and floats as plain text on the circle, the NEW FLAVOUR badge is squashed into an ellipse, and the badges and logo are scattered with no reading order. B keeps the original's structure and hierarchy, but it is mostly a shrunk copy: the ZERO SUGAR tag and the NEW FLAVOUR text are too small to read, the CTA and the FIZZBANG! logo are jammed against the bottom edge, and the circle crowds the right edge.

A keeps a clear headline→CTA hierarchy with a strong pink button, but the date card is shrunk to an illegible sliver (no SAT/NOV/time), the FIZZBANG logo and eyebrow are tiny, and a cropped pattern fragment floats awkwardly under the CTA with the controller jammed into the far-right corner. B is worse: an oversized, zoomed-in pattern block becomes the main focal point, the date card is an unreadable chip stranded at the far left, logo/controller/body copy are crammed under the headline with an orphaned 'pm.', and the eyebrow is microscopic and detached at the top right.

A breaks the flavour list apart: Lime/Mango/Grape sit at the top right, Cherry Bang is stranded bottom left and Cola Crash bottom right. The logo floats mid-left, the headline is buried beside the can, and the CTA is tiny and jammed in the bottom corner, so it has no reading order at all. B keeps a sensible top-to-bottom stack (logo, can, headline, list, CTA), but the list items shrink in size from row to row, are out of their original order and don't line up on the left. The logo pill and CTA are too small, everything is crammed into the upper two-thirds, and there is a large dead band at the bottom.

A keeps the original's centred two-line serif headline and adapts it well to the landscape canvas. Its flaw is that the type is scaled up so far that the side margins (~35px) and the vertical breathing room are much tighter than the original's quiet, generous whitespace, so it loses some of the 'silence' feel. B pushes the headline block into the upper-left with a ~30px left margin, leaving the right ~40% and bottom ~40% as dead space, so the layout is lopsided. Its centred-within-block alignment then looks arbitrary against the off-centre placement, which reads as a broken placement, not intent.

A: the quote is set small and the oversized logo block outweighs it, so the hierarchy is inverted. The attribution is detached far below at an illegible size, and dead bands sit above the quote mark and between the quote and the logo. B: the quote is properly the largest element, but the quote mark is oversized with a big empty gap beneath it. The logo is jammed right under the last line, and the attribution is again detached and microscopic. B is slightly better only because the quote leads.

A keeps the right reading order (logo, eyebrow, headline, body, CTA). But it drops the architectural photo completely. The headline breaks one word per line at an oversized scale, the centred logo and CTA don't line up with the left-aligned text, and the CTA sits cramped against the bottom edge. B scrambles the hierarchy: the CTA is stranded at the top above the brand, the logo is blown up until it competes with the headline, and 'NOW OPEN' falls below the body copy and is rendered heavier than the body copy. The photo shrinks to a meaningless strip at the bottom with dead space above it.

A breaks the reading order: the headline is squeezed into a narrow bottom-left column and touches the bottom edge, below the watch. The price block sits above everything, the logo is shrunk to a tiny mark floating mid-canvas, and the legal copy is as large as the subhead, so it competes with the message. B keeps a sensible order (headline, then price, subhead and CTA) in a clear right column, but the watch is cropped at the left and top edges. The CTA is oversized and nearly outweighs the headline, the logo is tiny in the bottom-left corner, and the legal text is unreadably small.

A keeps a sensible left-to-right order (headline → image → schedule → CTA), but the schedule is broken into scattered fragments in the wrong order (13 Jan, 02 Dec, 20 Jan, 06 Jan, 16 Dec), only '02 Dec / Printmaking' is readable, the dates and times are microscopic, the logo is gone, and the legal text is crammed illegibly next to the CTA. B is worse: the CTA sits first, on the far left, and overlaps the '20 Jan' and '16 Dec' rows; the logo shrinks to a tiny icon jammed beside '18:00'; the 'Winter Programme' label floats far to the right; the legal copy is bigger than the event list; and the schedule rows are scattered, unreadable fragments.

A drops the sea photo entirely (fidelity loss), centres the logo over left-aligned copy, wraps the subcopy into a cramped 4-line column, and makes the CTA so large it competes with the headline. Even so, it is legible and well structured. B crops the photo to a useless sky sliver and puts the white logo on pale sky, where it is almost invisible. It also leaves a large empty blue band in the middle and crams the headline, copy and CTA into the bottom, with the button jammed against the bottom edge.

A's hierarchy is inverted: the Meridian logo is far bigger than the small headline. The suitcase takes over the canvas, and the body copy, a tiny CTA and the sunglasses are crammed into one strip at the bottom edge. The pale circle is cropped there and runs into the suitcase wheels. B reads in a sensible order (headline, copy, suitcase, CTA), but the body copy is tiny and the CTA is undersized. The left-aligned headline clashes with the centred suitcase and CTA, there is dead space above the bottom row, and the logo sits squeezed next to the sunglasses on a cropped circle in the corner.

A: the Reykjavik card is shrunk to about half the size of the other two cards and pushed into the bottom-left corner, so the three cards no longer look like a set. The tagline and CTA float on a different axis next to it, with a big empty gap between the top two cards, and the logo sits awkwardly beside the headline. B: all three fare cards are shrunk to tiny scattered thumbnails whose 'from' labels can't be read, and the cards are spread across a mostly empty canvas. The CTA sits at the top, before the headline, which breaks the reading order, and the tagline is tiny and isolated. A is broken but B is unusable.

A has broken reading order. The badge, a tiny 'Find a Fare' CTA and the sunglasses are crammed into one row above the logo and headline, and the sunglasses run off the panel's right edge. The panel is jammed against the top and left canvas edges, the logo is oversized and there is a large dead gap between the logo and the headline. B keeps the headline at the top and gives the badge and CTA real prominence, but it still has clear flaws. The oversized logo straddles the panel's top edge with half of it sitting on the sky. The sunglasses are clipped at the panel's bottom edge, and the supporting copy has been pushed below the CTA, separated from its headline. B is still the less broken of the two.

A keeps a clean blue brand panel with the logo, headline and CTA, but the fare list is shrunk to tiny, barely legible text and scattered down the left in jumbled order. The legal line sits between the London/Vienna/Paris rows and the Rome/Berlin/Madrid rows, and Madrid drifts off the column. B is worse: the 'Vienna' row and a tiny 'Paris' row sit in dark text on the blue panel, so they are unreadable collisions. Fare rows switch between large and microscopic sizes, Paris's price is missing, the CTA straddles the panel edge, and the panel leaves a white strip along its top.

A is a near-uniform shrink of the original: structure, hierarchy and brand survive, but the 'ZERO SUGAR' and 'NEW FLAVOUR' badge text is now tiny, the bottom row sits tight to the edge, and nothing has really been rearranged for the format. B falls apart. The 'Grab a Can' CTA has lost its button and floats as plain text on the yellow circle. The can is shrunk and jammed against the top edge, the 'NEW FLAVOUR' badge is squashed into a distorted ellipse that collides with the circle edge, and the FIZZBANG logo drifts below the circle, so the reading order is jumbled and the product is no longer the focal point.

A: the date card is shrunk to an illegible speck at the far left, a big decorative pattern block takes the prime left-centre space, the 'FIZZBANG ARCADE NIGHT' eyebrow is a microscopic floating fragment above the CTA, the logo and controller are tiny chips, and the body copy wraps to leave 'pm.' orphaned. B: the headline leads strongly and the CTA is prominent, but the logo is a tiny chip jammed against the left edge, the date card is again an illegible sliver, the pattern strip is wedged under the CTA, the eyebrow and controller are microscopic, and the body copy is small and crammed against the right edge. B is the less bad of the two because its hierarchy and left-to-right reading order are clearer.

A keeps a sensible left-image/right-copy layout with the headline clearly dominant, but the watch strap is cropped at the top and left edges. The price is placed above the subhead (wrong order), the CTA is oversized, and the logo is shrunk to a speck jammed into the bottom-left beside illegibly tiny legal text. B is jumbled: the headline is pushed to the bottom-left and broken into four lines, the warranty fine print is set as large as body copy and becomes the biggest block, the price wraps awkwardly onto three lines next to the CTA, and the logo floats tiny in the middle, so there is no hierarchy or reading order.

A is unusable: the fare cards are shrunk to tiny scattered postage stamps with illegible city names and 'from' labels, Reykjavik is stranded far below the others, the subhead floats alone in empty space, and the CTA sits at the top above the headline, so there's huge dead space everywhere. B keeps the cards readable and the brand intact, but the Reykjavik card is a smaller, mismatched size jammed into the bottom-left corner, the two top cards are spaced unevenly with a big gap, the headline breaks to an orphaned 'out', and the CTA/subhead block doesn't line up with the cards.

A is broken. The CTA pill is at the very top, above the quote, so the reading order is reversed. The quote mark floats with a dead gap above a small one-line headline. The blush circle has come apart from the bottle and sits alone in the bottom-right corner, and the small bottle floats in empty space. B keeps a strong hierarchy: a large wrapped quote, and the bottle layered on the circle as in the original. Its flaws are a large empty gap between the quote mark and the headline, attribution and CTA crammed onto one row, the CTA pill pressing against the circle and bottle edge, and the bottle sitting off-centre on its circle.

A: the Shop pill runs off the right edge of the canvas, so the CTA is clipped, and the tiny Obsidian logo sits cramped on top of the product with almost no padding, although the one-line headline reads well. B: everything stays inside the canvas and the price sits grouped with a complete Shop button, but the headline is squeezed into two centred lines that fill the full 50px height, the logo is tiny and jammed against the top-left, and the price text right above the button is small and cramped.

A shrinks the OBSIDIAN logo to an illegible speck at the far left, which effectively loses the brand. Its text stack is jammed against the top and bottom edges, and the whole right half of the banner is dead space. B keeps the logo readable and anchored at the right, which balances the banner, but its 'Rated 5 out of 5' line is tiny. B's quote stack is also cramped vertically, with the quote mark almost touching the top edge, and the middle of the banner is a large empty gap.

A is basically a scaled-down copy of the square layout: the headline, CTA, ZERO SUGAR and FIZZBANG text are all too small to read, and the yellow circle has come loose from the can and drifted right, where it reads as a random blob with the NEW FLAVOUR badge stuck to it. There's also a lot of dead blue space. B actually rearranges for the banner: a big left-aligned headline, the logo top-left, and the can on the right with its yellow backdrop. But the Grab a Can CTA is small and gets lost in a row with the NEW FLAVOUR badge (squashed from a circle into a pill) and the ZERO SUGAR tag, so the button and the badges compete. The yellow circle is cropped and barely visible behind the can, and the bottom row is indented and doesn't line up with the headline's left edge.

A keeps the FIZZBANG! pill large and legible with clean margins, and the left-to-right layout suits the banner. But the pill sits off-centre, and the 'SINCE 2026' badge is pushed to the far right with a big dead gap between it and the pill, so it reads as a stray fragment rather than a grouped tagline. B is just the original shrunk: the pill is tiny in the middle of a huge empty halftone field, the wordmark is crammed against the pill outline, and the 'SINCE 2026' badge text is too small to read. Most of the canvas is wasted.

A shrinks the headline and drops it into the lower part of the canvas (block centered around 63% of the height). That leaves a large dead area at the top, the layout is lopsided, and the type looks timid for a single-message poster. B re-wraps to three lines at a strong size that fills the width with even side margins and centers it vertically, keeping the original's calm, centered feel. Its only small flaw is that the margins are a little tight relative to the original's generous white space.

A really does rearrange the layout for the square, but it has clear flaws. The 'EXHIBITION' kicker is stranded to the right of the photo, away from the headline it introduces, so the reading order breaks. The black date box is indented and doesn't line up with the left edge of the headline and photo. The logo floats without aligning to the box's right edge, and there is dead space beside the photo. B is just the original portrait poster dropped into the middle of the square, leaving wide empty white bands on the left and right. The photo no longer runs to the canvas edges. Nothing was rearranged for the new format, and all the content is shrunk into a centre column.

A: the quote is squeezed into a narrow column with an orphaned 'A' and choppy breaks. The attribution is cut off from its quote, sits below the logo and is set larger and bolder than the brand name, which wrecks the reading order and the hierarchy, and it crowds the bottom edge. B: the order and grouping are right (quote, then attribution, then logo), but the logo is far bigger than the small quote, so the hierarchy is inverted. The attribution runs almost edge to edge right under the quote, the quote mark floats small and alone, and the bottom third is dead space.

A: the oversized logo sits on the photo and its 'MONOGRAPH' wordmark runs into and is clipped by the white panel edge. The 'Plan a Visit' CTA is shrunk to a tiny pill jammed against the bottom edge, and 'NOW OPEN' is moved after the CTA, which breaks the reading order. B: the architectural photo is dropped entirely, a real loss of fidelity, and 'NOW OPEN' is crammed against the 'building' line of the headline. Still, B's headline, body copy and large CTA read clearly left to right with sound hierarchy.

A has a sensible three-column banner with the logo kept prominent, but the headline is broken into four lines with one word each ("the" stands alone), so it overwhelms the frame. The CTA is oversized, and the legal block is crammed against the CTA and the bottom edge. B is worse. The logo shrinks to an illegible stamp beside the legal text, the price is nearly as large as the headline and competes with it, and "warranty" and "m." are left as orphans. The centre stack is vertically cramped while the CTA floats far to the right, cut off from its copy.

A breaks the reading order: the list runs WED, THU, TUE, and the WED item floats above the headline, cut off from the other talks. The divider rules are left as orphaned stray lines, and the talk text is tiny, but the 'All free, all at 19:00.' line stays intact. B also splits the list (TUE above the headline, WED and THU at the bottom) and squeezes 'All free, all at 19:00.' into a narrow one-word-per-line column jammed beside THU. Its bottom-left corner is cramped and ragged, while the enlarged logo pulls focus from the headline.

A is just the banner's columns stretched vertically. The list items are spread far apart, with dead space between them and stray divider lines at the top and bottom; the 'All free' subline drifts far below its headline; and the logo and headline stay small, leaving large empty areas. Still, the reading order and grouping are intact. B scrambles the structure: TUE sits top-left, away from WED and THU, the headline is jammed into the top-right corner on top of a divider, 'All free' is wedged between WED and THU, and the oversized logo dominates the headline, so it is unusable.

A keeps the original's structure, hierarchy and left-to-right reading order intact, but it is basically the original dropped into a taller canvas: the content sits in a small middle band with dead space above and below, and the text is no bigger, so it under-uses the format. B actually rearranges the layout, but the logo is blown up to rival the headline and the reading order is broken: headline bottom-left, suitcase in the middle, then body copy and CTA jammed top-right. The CTA and sunglasses pile onto the circle, the sunglasses crowd the right edge, and the composition feels cramped and has no clear focal point.

A keeps the original's structure: a large quote, the bottle on its blush circle, and the attribution and CTA grouped together. Its flaws: the quote mark floats far above the headline with a big dead gap, the circle is offset low and clipped behind the bottle, and the CTA sits awkwardly next to the bottle. B breaks the design: the CTA and logo are jammed at the top above the quote, so the reading order is reversed. The blush circle is detached from the bottle and stranded in the bottom-right corner. The bottle is small and floats mid-canvas, the quote runs as one long line, and the bottom half is empty.

A reads cleanly left to right: logo and buds on the left, the two-line headline in the centre, and price above a pill Shop button on the right. Its flaws are a tiny logo, a cramped product icon, and a price line jammed against the top edge. B's Shop button has turned into a circle that is cut off at the right canvas edge and nearly touches the end of the headline, and its OBSIDIAN logo is shrunk until it is illegible. That leaves a broken CTA and a weak brand mark.

A: the headline is shrunk to roughly the size of the cyan source line, so it barely leads. The quote mark is a speck, 'Rated 5 out of 5' is near-illegible, and the text block floats off-centre with dead space at both ends. Its saving grace is a readable OBSIDIAN logo anchored on the right. B: the logo is shrunk to an unreadable smudge jammed against the left edge, so the brand is effectively lost. The text stack overfills the height: the quote mark touches the top, 'Rated 5 out of 5' sits on the bottom edge, and the line spacing is cramped. There is a big empty gap between the logo and the copy.

A shrinks the original into a small centred stack: the FIZZBANG! wordmark is jammed edge to edge inside its pill, with the F and ! touching the outline. The SINCE 2026 badge is tiny and hard to read, and the large empty halftone areas on both sides make it look like a shrunk square rather than a banner. B keeps a large pill with properly padded, legible headline text and reads left to right with the badge on the right. However, the pill sits at an arbitrary offset that is neither centred nor on a margin, it nearly touches the top and bottom edges, and the badge floats far away and disconnected near the right edge.

A: the NEW badge is cut off at the left and top edges. The headline wraps onto two cramped lines and the subcopy is squeezed into a narrow three-line column ('Whipped / fig and / shea, $38'). That reads poorly in a 320x50 banner, and the CTA is almost as big as the headline. B: the headline sits on one line with the subcopy under it, so the left-to-right order works. Its flaws are a NEW badge still clipped at the canvas edge, a tiny jar with an unreadable label, and an undersized Shop Now button pushed against the right edge.

A breaks the hierarchy: the attribution 'MAYA R., VERIFIED BUYER' is the biggest text and sits above the quote. The quote itself is squeezed into a narrow column at one or two words per line, and it crowds the giant bottle. The CTA sits up top, before the message, and the circle has become a stray fragment in the corner. B reads cleanly from logo to quote mark to quote to bottle to CTA. Its flaws: the attribution is heavier than the quote it credits, there is dead space between the quote mark and the quote, the bottle is small, and the peach circle is orphaned in the bottom-right corner, cut off and no longer behind the bottle.

A: the backdrop circle has drifted off the bottle and sits empty on the right. The cream jar has shrunk to an illegible icon jammed in the top-right corner, so a key product is effectively lost. 'THE NIGHT SET' has dropped below the body copy, and a dead band sits under the CTA. B: the serum bottle is oversized and dominates the left half. The cream jar is stranded at the bottom edge, away from the bottle. The circle's lower edge cuts through the 'Night Serum…' copy, the eyebrow is again misplaced below the copy, and the logo is tiny. Still, B keeps both products recognisable and has a coherent left-image/right-text split with a strong price and CTA.

In both, the circle is stretched into a tall ellipse, which distorts the brand shape, and the tagline is now much bigger than the 'Lumen & Fig' wordmark, so the hierarchy is upside down. The large 'Skincare,' also runs almost into the edges of the ellipse. A is worse: the logo is pushed up near the top, 'Fig' touches the ellipse edge, and a big empty gap cuts it off from the tagline. B keeps the logo closer to the tagline and inside the shape, so the lockup holds together better.

A is a shrunk portrait column in a wide canvas: the teal circle has come away from the headphones and sits alone at the right, the divider runs only on the right, the two stat columns are pushed far apart across a big empty gap, and the logo, subhead, stat labels and legal text are tiny. B has a strong left column (logo, headphones, large headline), but the right half is a mess: the stats are out of order and at random sizes (10 min is huge, the others small), 250 g and 6 mics sit on the leftover circle, the subhead floats at the top, and the legal text is as large as the copy next to a small CTA. B is still more readable and more intentional overall.

A keeps a sensible top-to-bottom order (eyebrow, headline, date card, headphones, copy and CTA), but the headphones' grey circle has come loose and sits behind the RSVP button as a stray shape. The date card is shrunk so that 'FRI, 7:30 PM' is barely readable, and the body copy is jammed against the CTA at the bottom. B is worse: the date card is a tiny chip where 'NOV' and the time can't be read, and the 'LISTENING SESSION' eyebrow has dropped below the headphones, which breaks the reading order. The loose circle also collides with the body copy in the bottom-right corner, and the small copy and CTA are crammed into the bottom while a large dead area opens up above.

A: the headline is oversized and runs onto the yellow circle, so the white 'here' sits on yellow with weak contrast. The can, the hero of the original, is shrunk to a small left-edge item, and the yellow circle no longer backs it. Can, CTA, badge, sticker and logo sit in one evenly weighted row, so nothing leads. Still, all text is readable and the CTA is clear. B: the yellow circle is split from the can and left as a large empty blob on the right, with the NEW FLAVOUR badge shrunk on top of it. ZERO SUGAR, the FIZZBANG! logo and the 'Grab a Can' CTA are tiny and hard to read at this size. The headline is small, there is dead space all around, and the placement looks random, so the layout does not work.

A reads left to right (logo → headline/list → can → CTA) with a readable CTA, but the flavour list is reordered (Cherry, Mango, Cola, Grape, Lime) and each item gets smaller, so 'Grape Pop' and 'Lime Zap' are tiny. The dots and labels are ragged and not aligned, and the logo is jammed near the left edge. B has the same shrinking, reordered list, which is even smaller and close to illegible. Its CTA is a microscopic, unreadable pill stranded at the bottom left, so the action is buried. The can runs off the bottom and right edges, and the logo, headline and list are crowded into the middle with no clear grid.

A reads left to right with a strong headline and a legible date block, but the 'Monograph Gallery, 4 / Kiln Lane' address breaks badly (the '4' is stranded at a line end) and is set as large as the dates, so it competes with them. The tiny 'EXHIBITION' label is stranded under the photo, and 'Poetry' almost touches the right edge. B is broken: the headline's 'C' runs into the photo, the date block is shrunk and its hours line can't be read, the logo is tiny, 'EXHIBITION' is jammed onto the end of the address line, and the right third of the canvas is empty.

A: the Meridian logo has been pulled out of the blue panel, shrunk, and left sitting on the busy green hill. The supporting copy is squeezed into a narrow five-line column jammed against the panel's right edge, and the sunglasses overlap the panel's corner. Its headline, badge and CTA still read left to right with a sizeable button. B: the oversized logo runs into the panel edge (the 'n' touches it) and the sunglasses are cropped at the top. The 'Find a Fare' CTA is shrunk to a tiny pill stuck onto the end of the subcopy, so the action is buried. A is the less broken of the two.

A: the card fills almost the whole canvas, so the leaf imagery is gone; the bottle is jammed against the left edge and cut by the card border; the 'NEW NIGHT SERUM' eyebrow ends up bottom-left under the logo, out of reading order; and the four loose columns don't group. B keeps the leaf-and-bottle panel and a clear headline → body → CTA flow, but the CTA nearly touches the end of the headline, and the logo plus the 'NEW NIGHT SERUM' eyebrow are shrunk to tiny, barely legible text at the bottom, which weakens the brand.

A breaks the step list apart: steps 2–4 are pushed against the left edge in tiny, unreadable text, and step 1 sits alone under the headline. That puts the list out of reading order, leaves big empty gaps on the left and makes the CTA look small and squeezed. B keeps the headline, logo, CTA and jar strong and the steps run 1→4 top to bottom, but step 1 is huge while steps 2–4 are tiny. The step 2–4 rows are also scattered on misaligned left edges (step 2 indented, step 4 offset), so the list has no grid and its fine text is near illegible.

A: step 1 is split off to the centre while steps 2–4 sit in a stack on the far left at a tiny, unreadable size, which breaks the sequence. The headline, CTA, jar and logo do read cleanly left to right. B is worse: the steps are scattered in the order 3/1/2/4 at mismatched sizes, step 4 is microscopic, the logo is shrunk to a speck above the headline and the jar is cropped at the right edge.

A shrinks the Obsidian logo until the wordmark can't be read, while the headline is blown up so far that it nearly touches the Shop button. The button is also jammed against the right edge with almost no margin, which leaves the layout cramped and lopsided. B keeps the logo legible and gives the headline sensible weight, with even gutters and a properly inset CTA; its only weaknesses are that it is close to a straight proportional shrink and the headline is a little small at this size.

A enlarges the headline but crams the date card, headphone circle, body copy and CTA into the right third: the body copy and the RSVP button sit on top of the headphone graphic, the headphones are cropped behind the card, and 'Listening Session' is shrunk to an unreadable caption under the card, which breaks the hierarchy and reading order. B is basically the original shrunk uniformly and nothing collides. Its flaws: the orphaned 'live' in the headline, small body and CTA text, and a wide empty left margin (~115px) with the content packed toward the right, so it reads as a shrink rather than a deliberate rearrangement.

Both put '$3' above '2 FOR', so the offer reads backwards, and both shrink the FIZZBANG logo to an illegible pill. A jams the can against the left edge, strands the CTA and logo far right, and leaves big dead gaps. B is worse because the CTA, logo and body copy are crammed into one run along the bottom edge, with the copy butting the logo and the can floating off to the side.

A inverts the hierarchy: the FIZZBANG! logo pill is shrunk to a tiny chip jammed against the left edge, while the secondary 'SINCE 2026' badge is blown up into the dominant element. B keeps the logo as the clear hero, but it is pushed to the far right, leaving a large dead halftone area on the left. The small 'SINCE 2026' badge floats low and to the left, not aligned with or grouped near the logo, so the composition looks arbitrary rather than designed.

A: the logo has been moved out of the card onto the busy photo, and the 'MONOGRAPH' wordmark runs under the card edge so the H is clipped. 'NOW OPEN' now sits below the body copy, which breaks the reading order, and the card is cut off at the top with a large dead white gap under the CTA. B keeps the right order (eyebrow, headline, body, CTA) with readable text on white, but the logo is blown up so far that it outweighs the headline. The wordmark also straddles the edge between photo and white, and the bottom text block is cramped, with the CTA nearly touching the right edge.

A: the oversized logo's 'GALLERY' wordmark runs into the top edge of the white card, which is a real collision. Inside the card, the 'NOW OPEN' eyebrow drops below the body copy, there is a big empty band above the headline, and the CTA is centred while all the text is left-aligned. B: the logo sits cleanly above the card with no collision, but it has the same problems inside the card. 'NOW OPEN' comes after the body copy, there is dead space at the top and bottom, and the CTA is indented about 35px from the text's left edge. The card also nearly touches the canvas edges, and the logo is so big that it outranks the headline.

A: the schedule rows are out of date order (09 Dec, 20 Jan, 02 Dec…), indented unevenly and set in mixed, tiny sizes. The legal copy is blown up into a ragged column the same weight as the CTA. The logo is a speck and the photo is cropped at the bottom. Even so, the headline→image→CTA structure reads.
